content:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle withdrew their two children from their previous school just two days into the academic year.

According to a report first published by Hello! magazine, 5-year-old Prince Archie and 3-year-old Princess Lili were withdrawn after the couple's private security team raised safety concerns.

The report indicated that Harry and Meghan's private security team pointed to heavy traffic near the school and a lengthy commute as potential risks for the family. Hello! also reported that there had been an occurrence which made it difficult for the family convoy to travel together.

A spokesperson for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex told HuffPost: "After discussions with the family's security team about whether the current arrangements were workable, a decision was made to transfer the children to another school."

The spokesperson added: "The parents are sincerely grateful to all the teachers and staff at the school for the love, care and effort they have consistently devoted to their family. This decision in no way reflects any negative view of the school, nor does it diminish the outstanding attention the children have always received from the school."

Since stepping back from royal duties, Harry has been stripped of government-funded police protection and has since continued to express concerns about security arrangements in the UK.

He once challenged the decision through legal proceedings, arguing that the arrangements placed him and his family at extreme risk.

In an interview with the BBC in May 2025, when the family was in the United States, Prince Harry said: "At this point I cannot imagine bringing my wife and children back to the UK."

The Daily Telegraph reported that, as they are currently in the UK, the Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC) will carry out a new official risk assessment for the couple.
